body:
Owning issue: https://github.com/beamfall/corvint/issues/388
Owner requested parallel implementation on 2026-09-30. Original issue intent follows; repository contracts and accepted authority remain governing.

## Summary

Make Corvint the system that keeps documentation, end-to-end tests, and follow-up work in step with every merged change. After a change request merges, one repeatable workflow should:

1. read the merged change, its description, and the linked work item with its parent hierarchy (for example, story → epic);
2. decide which documentation is stale, which behaviour lacks asserting tests, and what looks wrong;
3. open or update **one follow-up work item** that tracks the outcome;
4. open a **reviewable documentation change request**;
5. open a **reviewable test change request** for missing end-to-end coverage, with proof that the new tests are stable and actually assert;
6. **raise findings** (possible defects, scope mismatches, coverage gaps) where people triage them;
7. republish any derived corpus once the documentation change is approved.

Everything the workflow produces is a draft for human review at first. Specific content classes move to automatic merge only once measured correction rates earn it.

## Why Corvint

Most of the evidence engine already exists: revision binding (`status`, `record`, `witness`), drift detection (`docs flows check`), external evidence providers and fail-closed test selection (EEP-V0..V2, ETS-V0), test-validity receipts, `behavior-falsify`, and Tasks. PRS-V1-015 already requires automatic documentation that detects drift, previews updates, supports explicit apply, and never publishes itself. The product loop in `PRODUCT.md` ends with "merge-time independent re-verification → knowledge delta". Today every adopter has to assemble that loop by hand from CI YAML, scripts, and agent prompts, and each one invents its own containment, idempotency, and fail-closed rules.

## Scope boundary

Core stays as decision 0373 defines it: local, no network, no daemon, no authority. Anything that talks to a network, holds credentials, runs an agent, or writes to an external system belongs in a separately qualified companion, the way Tasks does. Core supplies deterministic, source-content-free records. The companion and the CI host act on them.

## Agnostic by design

- **Work tracker:** any tracker, through a connector contract. No tracker's field model is assumed.
- **Forge:** any forge that has change requests.
- **CI host:** any CI host. The trigger, runner, secrets, and schedule stay with the host.
- **Agents:** any coding agent. Corvint defines what an authoring step may read and write, and verifies it afterwards.
- **Stacks:** any language stack that Corvint's analyzers and providers cover.

## Sub-requests

- [ ] #389 corvint delta, one read-only source-content-free record for a merged change
- [ ] #390 range and path impact for non-Go languages (impact accepts only .go today)
- [ ] #391 closed-vocabulary intake for untrusted change context (descriptions, linked work items and their parents)
- [ ] #392 work-tracker and forge connector contract (read hierarchy, idempotent follow-up item, gated findings, draft change requests)
- [ ] #393 scope attestation for authoring agent steps in automated workflows
- [ ] #394 acceptance verdict for new end-to-end tests (repeat, falsify, validity in one record)
- [ ] #395 replay historical merges through the post-merge workflow with recorded writes
- [ ] #396 per-content-class evidence for earning automated merge
- [ ] #397 corpus republish from an approved documentation revision with provenance and parity
- [ ] #398 reference CI host templates and host adapter contract for the post-merge workflow
- [ ] #399 documentation corpus parity to replace bespoke corpus builders and servers

## Acceptance (for the umbrella)

- A reference workflow processes a merged change end to end with outward writes stubbed. It produces the follow-up item, the documentation change request, the test change request, and the findings as recorded requests, and it matches labelled expectations on a replay set.
- Replaying the same merge twice produces no duplicates.
- Untrusted text never reaches an authoring step except as validated closed-vocabulary fields.
- No authoring step can see a credential that performs an outward write.

Umbrella gap check 2026-10-05 at origin/main 8a35775a (lane claude/v1-0535-umbrella-acceptance; no code change; verdict CLOSE_WHEN_DEPS_LAND). Passing tests (go1.27.1, -count=1): internal/postmergeworkflow, postmergeconnector, intake, cmd/corvint-intake, stepverify, plus a focused postmergehost run.
(a) Proven: TestReplayActualRecording MATCH for follow-up and finding requests; TestReplayMismatchBasis; TestReplaySeparatesHumanVerifiedMismatches; PMC-V0-005. Missing: docs/test drafts through the workflow (PMR-V0-005 draft-scope-validation-unavailable; /1 follow-up-not-integrated; no /2 producer) and a historical replay set. Owners: V1-0542, and V1-0545 for the CI host run (PCH-V0-003/014).
(b) Proven: TestReplayTwiceIdenticalRecording, recording-not-idempotent refusal, PMC-V0-006/007. Missing: the repeat with drafts (V1-0542).
(c) Proven: binding/hash-only adapter Request; hostile title absent; PMC-V0-003; CVI-V0-005..007; TestNativeActualIntakeDeltaThenFollowUpRefusal. Missing: a real authoring consumer (V1-0542).
(d) Proven: environment sentinel in TestReplayActualRecording, ASS-V0-005, PCH-V0-007 TestAuthoringEnvironmentHasNoWriteCredential, TestHostEnvelopeCompleteEnvironment. Missing: physical isolation and a hosted run (V1-0545, PCH-V0-011/014).
When V1-0542 and V1-0545 land, rerun the replay over the historical set with drafts, twice, on the reference host, and record one evidence-only build-log entry mapping (a)-(d). The COVERAGE_UNKNOWN effects blocker remains.
